candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall test the effluent for toxicity in accordance with the provisions in this section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a mandatory WET monitoring obligation for effluent; whether this obligation applies to a given facility/outfall depends on interpreting this section's scope and cross-references.

Scopes which discharge point(s) the WET requirements and associated pass/fail criteria apply to; different readings of outfall applicability change which measurements are evaluated for limits and monitoring obligations.

Sets the effluent dilution threshold referenced in the acute test failure definition; a different critical dilution value would change whether reported WET results are treated as exceeding the applicable limit.

Specifies the dilution concentrations that must be tested to determine NOEC; different interpretation of the required series affects whether a test was properly conducted and how NOEC/pass-fail is computed.

candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines which species and EPA methods govern WET testing; interpretation of required species/methods (including 'latest version') changes what monitoring was required and how results are evaluated for compliance.

candidates.exact_span: SAMPLE TYPE                        Defined in PART I
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defers sample type (e.g., grab vs. composite, timing) to PART I; without resolving that cross-reference, applicability of WET monitoring, limit comparison, and missing-evidence classification for WET results cannot be established.

candidates.exact_span: The NOEC (No Observed Lethal Effect Concentration) is herein defined as the greatest effluent dilution at and below which lethality that is statistically different from the control (0% effluent) at the 95% confidence level does not occur.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines how NOEC is calculated from test data; different readings of this statistical definition change whether a reported WET result is classified as passing or failing the enforceable toxicity standard.

candidates.exact_span: Acute test failure is defined as a demonstration of a statistically significant lethal effect at test completion to a test species at or below the critical dilution
candidates.computation_change_reason: States the operative pass/fail criterion for acute WET compliance; interpretation of 'statistically significant lethal effect' and 'at or below the critical dilution' directly determines whether measurements exceed the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: Once initiated, all toxicity tests must be completed unless specific authority has been granted by EPA Region 6 or the State NPDES permitting authority.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Conditions when an initiated test counts as satisfactorily performed versus improperly terminated; affects whether monitoring was required to be completed and how incomplete tests are classified in missing-evidence analysis.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall repeat a test, including the control and all effluent dilutions, if the procedures and quality assurance requirements defined in the test methods or in this permit are not satisfied, including the following additional criteria:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes when WET results are invalid and must be repeated; whether repeat was required changes whether an available result can be used for limit comparison or must be treated as inadequate/missing evidence.
